source.text: וְהָיָה֩ כִֽי־יָבֹ֨אוּ עָלֶ֜יךָ כָּל־הַדְּבָרִ֣ים הָאֵ֗לֶּה הַבְּרָכָה֙ וְהַקְּלָלָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר נָתַ֖תִּי לְפָנֶ֑יךָ וַהֲשֵׁבֹתָ֙ אֶל־לְבָבֶ֔ךָ בְּכָל־הַגּוֹיִ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֧ר הִדִּיחֲךָ֛ יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ שָֽׁמָּה׃

records.literal_gloss: And it will be, when come upon you all the things the these, the blessing and the curse that I have set before you, and you bring [them] back to your heart among all the nations where has driven you Yahweh your God there,

en.L: And it shall be, when all these things come upon you, the blessing and the curse that I have set before you, and you bring [them] back to your heart among all the nations where {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God has driven you,
en.B: When all these things have come upon you, the blessing and the curse that I have set before you, and you take them to heart among all the nations where {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God has driven you,
en.R: A time will come when all these things have happened to you, the blessings and the curses I have set before you. Then, in all the nations where {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God has driven you, you will think deeply about them.

vi.L: Và sẽ xảy ra, khi mọi điều này đến trên ngươi, phước lành và sự nguyền rủa mà tôi đã đặt trước mặt ngươi, và ngươi nhớ lại [chúng] trong lòng giữa mọi dân tộc nơi {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của ngươi đã đuổi ngươi đến,
vi.B: Khi mọi điều ấy đã xảy đến cho anh em, cả phước lành lẫn sự nguyền rủa mà tôi đã đặt trước mặt anh em, và anh em suy nghĩ kỹ trong lòng khi đang ở giữa các dân tộc mà {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của anh em đã đuổi anh em đến,
vi.R: Rồi sẽ đến lúc mọi điều ấy xảy ra cho anh em, cả những phước lành lẫn những sự nguyền rủa mà tôi đã đặt trước mặt anh em. Khi ấy, đang ở giữa các dân tộc mà {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của anh em đã đuổi anh em đến, anh em sẽ suy nghĩ thật kỹ về những điều đó.

decisions.choice: Moses is still speaking: the speech that began at 29:1 runs to the end of this chapter
decisions.reason: The words of chapter 30 are the last part of the speech the narrator introduced at 29:1. It ends at verse 20; chapter 31 returns to the story.

decisions.choice: the blessing and the curse: the two outcomes set out in chapters 27-28
decisions.reason: Moses has set both before the people (11:26-28; 28:1-68). He speaks of a time when both will have been lived through: the good years in the land and then the curses, ending in exile among the nations (28:64; 29:27).

decisions.choice: bring back to your heart: think it over, take it to heart
decisions.reason: To bring something back to the heart is to recall it and think it through until it changes one's mind (4:39; 1 Kings 8:47). The verb is "turn" or "return", which runs through verses 1-10: Israel turns its mind, turns back to the LORD (verses 2, 8, 10), and the LORD turns to restore and rejoice over them (verses 3, 9).

decisions.choice: and it shall be, when: the start of a long promise
decisions.reason: The opening looks ahead to a sure future. Verses 1-2 say what Israel will do when the curses have come; from verse 3 Moses says what the LORD will do in answer.

decisions.choice: no opening quotation mark
decisions.reason: The double quotation mark that opened Moses' speech at 29:1 stays open until it closes at the end of verse 20, so this record has none.

decisions.choice: take them to heart / think deeply about them
decisions.reason: Balanced uses the common English idiom for the same thought; Readable says it plainly. Literal keeps "bring back to your heart" so the repeated verb can be seen.

decisions.choice: "nhớ lại [chúng] trong lòng" for "bring back to your heart"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew idiom means to think something over; a word-for-word "bring back" is not Vietnamese.

source.text: וְשַׁבְתָּ֞ עַד־יְהוָ֤ה אֱלֹהֶ֨יךָ֙ וְשָׁמַעְתָּ֣ בְקֹל֔וֹ כְּכֹ֛ל אֲשֶׁר־אָנֹכִ֥י מְצַוְּךָ֖ הַיּ֑וֹם אַתָּ֣ה וּבָנֶ֔יךָ בְּכָל־לְבָבְךָ֖ וּבְכָל־נַפְשֶֽׁךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: and you return to Yahweh your God and listen to his voice according to all that I [am] commanding you this day, you and your sons, with all your heart and with all your soul,

en.L: and you return to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God and listen to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} voice according to all that I [am] commanding you today, you and your {{gender:children|sons}}, with all your heart and with all your soul,
en.B: and you and your {{gender:children|sons}} turn back to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God and obey {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} with all your heart and with all your soul, doing all that I command you today,
en.R: You and your {{gender:children|sons}} will come back to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God. You will obey {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} with all your heart and with all your being, and do everything I am commanding you today.

vi.L: và ngươi quay về với {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của ngươi và nghe theo tiếng {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, theo mọi điều tôi truyền cho ngươi hôm nay, ngươi và con cái ngươi, với hết lòng ngươi và với hết linh hồn ngươi,
vi.B: và anh em cùng con cái mình quay về với {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của anh em, hết lòng hết linh hồn vâng theo {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, làm đúng mọi điều tôi truyền cho anh em hôm nay,
vi.R: Anh em và con cái mình sẽ quay về với {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của anh em. Anh em sẽ vâng lời {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} với cả tấm lòng và cả con người mình, và làm mọi điều tôi truyền cho anh em hôm nay.

decisions.choice: return: turn back to God, repent
decisions.reason: The verb means to turn around. Turning back to the LORD after going after other gods is repentance, as Moses already foresaw in 4:30.

decisions.choice: listen to his voice: obey him
decisions.reason: To listen to someone's voice in Hebrew is to do what they say (4:30).

decisions.choice: you and your children: the whole people, parents and the next generation
decisions.reason: The words stand after "today" and spell out who is meant by "you": those who hear Moses and their children after them, all of whom will turn back.

decisions.choice: with all your heart and all your soul: with the whole person
decisions.reason: Heart is mind and will; soul is the self, one's very life. Together they mean with everything one is (4:29; 6:5).

decisions.choice: you and your children placed first, as the ones who turn back
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable move the phrase to the start of the clause, so it is clear that it names who returns. Balanced and Readable say "obey him" for the idiom.

decisions.choice: whole being / all your being
decisions.reason: As in 6:5, Balanced and Readable avoid "soul", which suggests to many readers only an inner, spiritual part, while the Hebrew means the whole living self. Literal keeps "soul".

decisions.choice: "quay về" for "return" (shuv) in verses 2, 8 and 10
decisions.reason: The Hebrew pictures turning back on the way; "quay về" keeps the picture and the sense of repentance.

source.text: וְשָׁ֨ב יְהוָ֧ה אֱלֹהֶ֛יךָ אֶת־שְׁבוּתְךָ֖ וְרִחֲמֶ֑ךָ וְשָׁ֗ב וְקִבֶּצְךָ֙ מִכָּל־הָ֣עַמִּ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֧ר הֱפִֽיצְךָ֛ יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ שָֽׁמָּה׃

records.literal_gloss: then will turn Yahweh your God your fortunes and have compassion on you, and he will return and gather you from all the peoples where has scattered you Yahweh your God there.

en.L: then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God will restore your fortunes and have compassion on you, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will return and gather you from all the peoples where {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God has scattered you.
en.B: then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God will restore your fortunes and have compassion on you. He will gather you again from all the peoples among whom {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God has scattered you.
en.R: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God will make things good for you again. He will have mercy on you. He will gather you again from all the nations where {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God has scattered you.

vi.L: thì {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của ngươi sẽ đổi lại vận mệnh ngươi và thương xót ngươi; {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sẽ lại thu nhóm ngươi từ mọi dân tộc nơi {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của ngươi đã phân tán ngươi.
vi.B: thì {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của anh em sẽ phục hồi vận mệnh anh em và thương xót anh em. Ngài sẽ thu nhóm anh em trở lại từ mọi dân tộc mà {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của anh em đã phân tán anh em đến.
vi.R: Bấy giờ {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của anh em sẽ làm cho anh em được tốt đẹp trở lại. Ngài sẽ thương xót anh em. Ngài sẽ thu nhóm anh em trở lại từ mọi nước mà {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của anh em đã phân tán anh em đến.

decisions.choice: restore your fortunes: turn your situation around
decisions.reason: The phrase repeats one root: "turn your turning". It is used of a full change from ruin to well-being (Job 42:10, of Job's losses; Psalm 126:4). Some take the noun as "captivity", "bring back your captives", which suits the exile in view here; the rest of the verse speaks of gathering the scattered either way.

decisions.choice: he will return and gather: he will gather again
decisions.reason: Joined to another verb, "return" often means doing something again. Here it also carries on the repeated word of verses 1-10: as Israel turns back, so the LORD turns back to them.

decisions.choice: have compassion: tender, deep-felt mercy
decisions.reason: The verb is related to the word for womb and speaks of the love of a parent for a child. Moses has already said that the LORD is a compassionate God who will not forget the covenant (4:31).

decisions.choice: make things good for you again; have mercy
decisions.reason: Readable says what "restore your fortunes" means in plain words, and uses the common word "mercy" for compassion.

source.text: אִם־יִהְיֶ֥ה נִֽדַּחֲךָ֖ בִּקְצֵ֣ה הַשָּׁמָ֑יִם מִשָּׁ֗ם יְקַבֶּצְךָ֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ וּמִשָּׁ֖ם יִקָּחֶֽךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: If is your banished [one] at [the] end of the heavens, from there will gather you Yahweh your God, and from there he will take you.

en.L: If your banished [ones] are at the end of the heavens, from there {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God will gather you, and from there {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will take you.
en.B: Even if you have been driven out to the farthest edge of the sky, from there {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God will gather you up, and from there {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will take you back.
en.R: You may have been sent away to the farthest place under the sky. Even so, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God will gather you from there and bring you back.

vi.L: Dù những người bị đày của ngươi ở tận cùng trời, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của ngươi cũng sẽ thu nhóm ngươi từ đó, và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sẽ đem ngươi về từ đó.
vi.B: Dù anh em có bị đuổi đến tận chân trời, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của anh em cũng sẽ thu nhóm anh em từ đó và đem anh em trở về.
vi.R: Có thể anh em đã bị đưa đến nơi xa nhất dưới bầu trời. Dù vậy, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của anh em vẫn sẽ thu nhóm anh em từ nơi đó và đem anh em trở về.

decisions.choice: the end of the heavens: the farthest edge of the world
decisions.reason: The sky was pictured as resting on the earth at its edges, so "the end of the heavens" is as far away as a land can be (4:32). Nehemiah takes up this promise in his prayer (Nehemiah 1:9).

decisions.choice: your banished one: any of your people who have been driven out
decisions.reason: The word is singular, "your driven-out one", but it means everyone of Israel who has been scattered, as the plural "you" of the promise shows.

decisions.choice: take you: fetch you, bring you back
decisions.reason: The common verb "take" here means to go and get someone from a place, the reverse of the scattering.

decisions.choice: even if; bring you back
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable bring out the force of "if" here, "no matter how far", and give the sense of "take" in this setting.

source.text: וֶהֱבִֽיאֲךָ֞ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֗יךָ אֶל־הָאָ֛רֶץ אֲשֶׁר־יָרְשׁ֥וּ אֲבֹתֶ֖יךָ וִֽירִשְׁתָּ֑הּ וְהֵיטִֽבְךָ֥ וְהִרְבְּךָ֖ מֵאֲבֹתֶֽיךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And will bring you Yahweh your God into the land that took possession of your fathers, and you will take possession of it, and he will do good to you and multiply you more than your fathers.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God will bring you into the land that your fathers took possession of, and you will take possession of it; and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will do you good and multiply you more than your fathers.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} your God will bring you into the land your ancestors took possession of, and you will take possession of it. He will make you more prosperous and more numerous than your ancestors.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} your God will bring you back into the land your ancestors took as their own, and you will take possession of it again. He will make you better off than your ancestors were, and there will be more of you than there were of them.

vi.L: Và {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của ngươi sẽ đem ngươi vào xứ mà tổ phụ ngươi đã chiếm hữu, và ngươi sẽ chiếm hữu nó; {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sẽ làm điều tốt cho ngươi và làm cho ngươi gia tăng hơn tổ phụ ngươi.
vi.B: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của anh em sẽ đem anh em vào xứ mà tổ tiên anh em đã chiếm hữu, và anh em sẽ chiếm lấy xứ ấy. Ngài sẽ làm cho anh em thịnh vượng và đông đúc hơn tổ tiên anh em.
vi.R: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của anh em sẽ đem anh em trở về xứ mà tổ tiên anh em đã chiếm làm của mình, và anh em sẽ chiếm lại xứ ấy. Ngài sẽ làm cho anh em sung túc hơn tổ tiên anh em, và dân số anh em sẽ đông hơn họ.

decisions.choice: the land your fathers possessed: the return repeats the first entry
decisions.reason: "Your fathers" here are the earlier generations who took the land under Joshua and lived in it before the exile. Going back is pictured as a second taking of the same land.

decisions.choice: do you good and multiply you: the curse of 28:63 reversed
decisions.reason: In 28:63 Moses warned that as the LORD had delighted to do Israel good and multiply them, so he would delight to destroy them. Here and in verse 9 the same words turn back to blessing.

decisions.choice: more than your fathers: goes with both verbs
decisions.reason: Israel will be both better off and more numerous than the generations before.

decisions.choice: ancestors
decisions.reason: As in 4:1, the Hebrew "fathers" means the forebears of the people. Balanced and Readable say "ancestors"; Literal keeps "fathers".

decisions.choice: bring you back ... take possession of it again
decisions.reason: Readable adds "back" and "again" to make clear that this is a return to a land Israel once held, as verses 3-4 say.

source.text: וּמָ֨ל יְהוָ֧ה אֱלֹהֶ֛יךָ אֶת־לְבָבְךָ֖ וְאֶת־לְבַ֣ב זַרְעֶ֑ךָ לְאַהֲבָ֞ה אֶת־יְהוָ֧ה אֱלֹהֶ֛יךָ בְּכָל־לְבָבְךָ֥ וּבְכָל־נַפְשְׁךָ֖ לְמַ֥עַן חַיֶּֽיךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And will circumcise Yahweh your God your heart and [the] heart of your offspring, to love Yahweh your God with all your heart and with all your soul, for the sake of your life.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God will circumcise your heart and the heart of your offspring, to love {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God with all your heart and with all your soul, so that you may live.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} your God will circumcise your heart and the hearts of your descendants, so that you love {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God with all your heart and with all your soul, and so live.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} your God will circumcise your hearts, and also the hearts of all who come after you. He will open them, so that you love {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God with all your heart and with all your being. Then you will live.

vi.L: Và {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của ngươi sẽ cắt bì lòng ngươi và lòng dòng dõi ngươi, để ngươi yêu kính {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của ngươi với hết lòng ngươi và với hết linh hồn ngươi, để ngươi được sống.
vi.B: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của anh em sẽ cắt bì lòng anh em và lòng dòng dõi anh em, để anh em hết lòng hết linh hồn yêu kính {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của anh em, và nhờ đó được sống.
vi.R: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của anh em sẽ cắt bì lòng anh em, và cả lòng của những người đến sau anh em. Ngài sẽ mở lòng anh em ra, để anh em yêu kính {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của anh em với cả tấm lòng và cả con người mình. Khi ấy anh em sẽ được sống.

decisions.choice: the LORD will circumcise your heart: what 10:16 commanded, the LORD now does
decisions.reason: In 10:16 Moses told Israel, "circumcise the foreskin of your heart". Here the LORD promises to do it himself, after the exile, for them and their children. The prophets take up the same hope of a new heart given by God (Jeremiah 31:33; 32:39; Ezekiel 36:26), and Paul speaks of circumcision of the heart by the Spirit (Romans 2:29).

decisions.choice: circumcise the heart: remove what closes the heart to God
decisions.reason: Circumcision was the sign of the covenant on the body (Genesis 17:10-14). An uncircumcised heart is closed and unwilling to hear (Leviticus 26:41; Jeremiah 4:4). To circumcise it is to open it fully to the LORD.

decisions.choice: to love: the purpose and result of the change
decisions.reason: The LORD changes the heart so that his people will love him wholly, as 6:5 commands. The command that Israel could not keep is made possible by what God does.

decisions.choice: for the sake of your life: so that you may live
decisions.reason: Life is the goal, the life with God in the land that verses 15-20 set before the people.

decisions.choice: descendants / all who come after you
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "seed" means offspring of every generation after. Balanced says "descendants" and Readable "all who come after you"; Literal says "offspring".

decisions.choice: He will open them
decisions.reason: Readable keeps the picture of circumcision and says what it means, as at 10:16.

decisions.choice: "yêu kính" for loving the LORD
decisions.reason: As Joshua 22:5 has it: love joined with reverence, the word Vietnamese uses for loving God.

source.text: וְנָתַן֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ אֵ֥ת כָּל־הָאָל֖וֹת הָאֵ֑לֶּה עַל־אֹיְבֶ֥יךָ וְעַל־שֹׂנְאֶ֖יךָ אֲשֶׁ֥ר רְדָפֽוּךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And will put Yahweh your God all the oaths the these on your enemies and on those hating you who pursued you.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God will put all these curses on your enemies and on those who hate you, who pursued you.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} your God will lay all these curses on your enemies, the people who hate you and persecuted you.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} your God will make all these curses fall on your enemies instead, on the people who hate you and hunted you down.

vi.L: Và {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của ngươi sẽ đặt mọi sự nguyền rủa này trên các kẻ thù của ngươi và trên những kẻ ghét ngươi, là những kẻ đã bắt bớ ngươi.
vi.B: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của anh em sẽ giáng mọi sự nguyền rủa này trên kẻ thù của anh em, là những kẻ ghét và bắt bớ anh em.
vi.R: Thay vào đó, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của anh em sẽ giáng mọi sự nguyền rủa này trên kẻ thù của anh em, là những kẻ ghét anh em và đã săn đuổi anh em.

decisions.choice: curses: the curses sworn in the covenant oath
decisions.reason: The word means an oath with a curse attached to it, the curse that falls on one who breaks a sworn covenant. It is the word used of the covenant oath in 29:11, 13 and of its curses in 29:19-20.

decisions.choice: on your enemies: the promise to Abraham
decisions.reason: The LORD promised Abraham that he would curse anyone who cursed him (Genesis 12:3). Once Israel is restored, the curses it suffered pass to the nations that hated and hunted it.

decisions.choice: pursued: chased down, persecuted
decisions.reason: The verb means to run after someone, and so to hunt down or persecute. It looks back on how the nations treated Israel in its exile.

decisions.choice: instead
decisions.reason: Readable adds "instead" to make clear the contrast with verse 1, where the curses came on Israel.

source.text: וְאַתָּ֣ה תָשׁ֔וּב וְשָׁמַעְתָּ֖ בְּק֣וֹל יְהוָ֑ה וְעָשִׂ֨יתָ֙ אֶת־כָּל־מִצְוֺתָ֔יו אֲשֶׁ֛ר אָנֹכִ֥י מְצַוְּךָ֖ הַיּֽוֹם׃

records.literal_gloss: And you, you will return and listen to [the] voice of Yahweh and do all his commandments that I [am] commanding you this day.

en.L: And you, you will return and listen to the voice of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and do all {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} commandments that I [am] commanding you today.
en.B: As for you, you will turn back and obey {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and keep all {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} commandments that I am giving you today.
en.R: And you will come back and obey {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. You will do all {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} commands that I am giving you today.

vi.L: Còn chính ngươi, ngươi sẽ quay về và nghe theo tiếng {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, và làm theo mọi điều răn của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} mà tôi truyền cho ngươi hôm nay.
vi.B: Còn anh em, anh em sẽ quay về, vâng theo {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} và giữ mọi điều răn của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} mà hôm nay tôi truyền cho anh em.
vi.R: Và anh em sẽ quay về vâng lời {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}. Anh em sẽ làm theo mọi điều răn của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} mà hôm nay tôi truyền cho anh em.

decisions.choice: and you: stress on Israel, in contrast with the enemies
decisions.reason: The pronoun is added for emphasis. While the curses fall on the enemies (verse 7), Israel itself will turn back and obey.

decisions.choice: you will return and listen: you will turn back, or you will again obey
alternatives: you will again obey the voice of the LORD
decisions.reason: As in verse 3, "return" joined to another verb can mean "again": "you will again listen to the voice of the LORD". Either way the verse repeats the turning of verse 2, now as a promise of what Israel will do.

decisions.choice: listen to the voice: obey
decisions.reason: As in verse 2.

decisions.choice: obey; keep / do
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of "listen to the voice". Literal keeps the Hebrew wording.

source.text: וְהוֹתִֽירְךָ֩ יְהוָ֨ה אֱלֹהֶ֜יךָ בְּכֹ֣ל׀מַעֲשֵׂ֣ה יָדֶ֗ךָ בִּפְרִ֨י בִטְנְךָ֜ וּבִפְרִ֧י בְהֶמְתְּךָ֛ וּבִפְרִ֥י אַדְמָתְךָ֖ לְטוֹבָ֑ה כִּ֣י׀יָשׁ֣וּב יְהוָ֗ה לָשׂ֤וּשׂ עָלֶ֨יךָ֙ לְט֔וֹב כַּאֲשֶׁר־שָׂ֖שׂ עַל־אֲבֹתֶֽיךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And will make you abound Yahweh your God in all [the] work of your hand, in [the] fruit of your womb and in [the] fruit of your livestock and in [the] fruit of your ground, for good; for will turn Yahweh to rejoice over you for good, as he rejoiced over your fathers,

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God will make you abound in all the work of your hand, in the fruit of your womb and in the fruit of your livestock and in the fruit of your ground, for good; for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will again rejoice over you for good, as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} rejoiced over your fathers,
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} your God will give you plenty in all that you do, in the children you bear, the young of your livestock and the crops of your soil, for your good. For {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will once more take delight in doing you good, as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} took delight in your ancestors,
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} your God will make everything you do succeed. He will give you many children, many young animals and good crops. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will again be glad to do good to you, just as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was glad over your ancestors.

vi.L: Và {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của ngươi sẽ làm cho ngươi dư dật trong mọi công việc tay ngươi, trong bông trái của lòng dạ ngươi, trong bông trái của súc vật ngươi và trong hoa quả của đất ngươi, để được tốt lành; vì {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} sẽ lại vui thích về ngươi để làm điều tốt, như {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã vui thích về tổ phụ ngươi,
vi.B: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của anh em sẽ cho anh em dư dật trong mọi việc anh em làm, trong con cái anh em sinh ra, trong súc vật con và hoa màu của đất đai anh em, vì lợi ích của anh em. Vì {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} sẽ lại vui thích làm điều tốt cho anh em, như {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã vui thích về tổ tiên anh em,
vi.R: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của anh em sẽ làm cho mọi việc anh em làm được thành công. Ngài sẽ cho anh em nhiều con cái, nhiều súc vật con và mùa màng tốt tươi. {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} sẽ lại vui lòng làm điều tốt cho anh em, như {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã vui lòng về tổ tiên anh em.

decisions.choice: fruit of your womb, livestock and ground: children, young animals and crops
decisions.reason: "Fruit" is what grows from something. The list repeats the blessings of 28:4 and 28:11, now given again after the exile.

decisions.choice: the LORD will again rejoice over you for good: 28:63 turned around
decisions.reason: In 28:63 the LORD who had rejoiced to do Israel good would rejoice to destroy them. Now he turns once more to rejoice in doing them good.

decisions.choice: turn to rejoice: rejoice again
decisions.reason: As in verse 3, "turn" with another verb means doing something again. It is another use of the word that runs through verses 1-10.

decisions.choice: for good: for your well-being
decisions.reason: "Good" here is prosperity and well-being, the good life in the land (verse 15).

decisions.choice: all that you do; children, young animals, crops
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "the work of your hand" and the three kinds of "fruit" mean, as at 7:13. Literal keeps the pictures.

decisions.choice: a new sentence at the end
decisions.reason: Readable ends the sentence here and starts verse 10 with "This will happen if", to keep the long Hebrew sentence readable.

source.text: כִּ֣י תִשְׁמַ֗ע בְּקוֹל֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ לִשְׁמֹ֤ר מִצְוֺתָיו֙ וְחֻקֹּתָ֔יו הַכְּתוּבָ֕ה בְּסֵ֥פֶר הַתּוֹרָ֖ה הַזֶּ֑ה כִּ֤י תָשׁוּב֙ אֶל־יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ בְּכָל־לְבָבְךָ֖ וּבְכָל־נַפְשֶֽׁךָ׃פ

records.literal_gloss: if you listen to [the] voice of Yahweh your God, to keep his commandments and his statutes, the written [thing] in [the] book of the law the this, if you return to Yahweh your God with all your heart and with all your soul.

en.L: if you listen to the voice of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, to keep {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} commandments and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} statutes that [are] written in this book of the law, if you return to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God with all your heart and with all your soul.
en.B: if you obey {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God and keep {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} commandments and statutes, as they are recorded in this book of the law, and if you turn back to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God with all your heart and with all your soul.
en.R: This will happen if you obey {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God and keep {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} commands and laws written in this book of teaching. It will happen if you come back to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God with all your heart and with all your being.

vi.L: nếu ngươi nghe theo tiếng {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của ngươi, để giữ các điều răn {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} và các luật lệ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã chép trong sách luật pháp này, nếu ngươi quay về với {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của ngươi với hết lòng ngươi và với hết linh hồn ngươi.
vi.B: nếu anh em vâng theo {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của anh em, giữ các điều răn và luật lệ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã chép trong sách luật pháp này, và nếu anh em hết lòng hết linh hồn quay về với {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của anh em.
vi.R: Điều đó sẽ xảy ra nếu anh em vâng lời {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của anh em và giữ các điều răn và luật lệ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã chép trong sách lời dạy này. Điều đó sẽ xảy ra nếu anh em quay về với {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của anh em với cả tấm lòng và cả con người mình.

decisions.choice: if ... if: the conditions of the promise
alternatives: when you obey ... when you return
because you obey ... because you return
decisions.reason: The word can mean "if", "when" or "because". Verses 1-2 already say that Israel will turn back, so it could be read "when" or "because you obey". Read as "if", it repeats that the blessing of verses 3-9 comes with obeying and returning.

decisions.choice: this book of the law: Moses' teaching written down
decisions.reason: "Law" here is the whole of what Moses teaches, not only rules (1:5). The phrase names that teaching as a written book (28:58, 61; 29:20); 31:9 and 31:24-26 tell how Moses wrote it and gave it to the priests.

decisions.choice: the written one: each command, or the whole as one
decisions.reason: "Written" is singular. It may refer to the commandments and statutes taken together as one body of teaching.

decisions.choice: This will happen if ... It will happen if
decisions.reason: Readable starts a new sentence for the conditions, after closing verse 9, and repeats the link to make clear what depends on them.

decisions.choice: teaching
decisions.reason: As elsewhere in Deuteronomy, Readable says "teaching" for the law Moses gives. Literal and Balanced keep "law".

source.text: כִּ֚י הַמִּצְוָ֣ה הַזֹּ֔את אֲשֶׁ֛ר אָנֹכִ֥י מְצַוְּךָ֖ הַיּ֑וֹם לֹֽא־נִפְלֵ֥את הִוא֙ מִמְּךָ֔ וְלֹ֥א רְחֹקָ֖ה הִֽוא׃

records.literal_gloss: For the commandment the this that I [am] commanding you this day, not [is] too wonderful it for you, and not far [is] it.

en.L: For this commandment that I [am] commanding you today, it [is] not too hard for you, and it [is] not far off.
en.B: For this commandment that I am giving you today is not too difficult for you, nor is it out of reach.
en.R: The command I am giving you today is not too hard for you. It is not far away from you.

vi.L: Vì điều răn này mà tôi truyền cho ngươi hôm nay, nó không quá khó cho ngươi, và nó không ở xa.
vi.B: Vì điều răn tôi truyền cho anh em hôm nay không quá khó đối với anh em, cũng không ở ngoài tầm tay anh em.
vi.R: Điều răn tôi truyền cho anh em hôm nay không quá khó cho anh em. Nó không ở xa anh em.

decisions.choice: this commandment: the whole charge Moses gives, taken as one
decisions.reason: "Commandment" is singular, as in 6:1 and 8:1. It sums up all Moses has taught: to love the LORD and keep his ways (verse 16).

decisions.choice: too wonderful: beyond one's power to understand or do
decisions.reason: The verb is used of what is too hard or too marvelous for someone (17:8; Genesis 18:14). God's command is not a riddle beyond human reach.

decisions.choice: for: the reason the promise of verses 1-10 can come true
decisions.reason: Verses 11-14 explain why Israel can turn back and obey: the command has been given plainly and is close at hand.

decisions.choice: out of reach
decisions.reason: Balanced says "out of reach" for "far", the point of the picture that verses 12-13 develop. Literal and Readable say "far".

source.text: לֹ֥א בַשָּׁמַ֖יִם הִ֑וא לֵאמֹ֗ר מִ֣י יַעֲלֶה־לָּ֤נוּ הַשָּׁמַ֨יְמָה֙ וְיִקָּחֶ֣הָ לָּ֔נוּ וְיַשְׁמִעֵ֥נוּ אֹתָ֖הּ וְנַעֲשֶֽׂנָּה׃

records.literal_gloss: Not in the heavens [is] it, to say, who will go up for us to the heavens and take it for us and make us hear it, and we will do it?

en.L: It [is] not in the heavens, to say, 'Who will go up for us to the heavens and take it for us and make us hear it, so that we may do it?'
en.B: It is not in heaven, that you would need to ask, 'Who will climb up to heaven for us and get it for us, and tell it to us so that we can do it?'
en.R: It is not up in heaven. You do not need to ask, 'Who will go up to heaven to get it for us? Who will tell it to us so we can obey it?'

vi.L: Nó không ở trên trời, để [ngươi] nói: 'Ai sẽ lên trời cho chúng ta và lấy nó cho chúng ta, và cho chúng ta nghe nó, để chúng ta làm theo?'
vi.B: Nó không ở trên trời, để anh em phải hỏi: 'Ai sẽ lên trời lấy nó xuống cho chúng ta, và nói cho chúng ta nghe để chúng ta làm theo?'
vi.R: Nó không ở tận trên trời. Anh em không cần phải hỏi: 'Ai sẽ lên trời lấy nó cho chúng ta? Ai sẽ nói cho chúng ta biết để chúng ta vâng theo?'

decisions.choice: not in heaven: no one has to make an impossible journey to get it
decisions.reason: Heaven, the sky above, and the far side of the sea (verse 13) were the farthest places anyone could think of. The point is that God's command is not hidden in some place only a hero could reach and bring back.

decisions.choice: used by Paul in Romans 10:6-8
decisions.reason: Paul quotes verses 12-14 and applies them to Christ and to "the word of faith" that is proclaimed: no one needs to go up to heaven to bring Christ down, because the word is near (Romans 10:6-8).

decisions.choice: make us hear it: tell it to us, proclaim it
decisions.reason: The verb is the causative of "hear": to cause someone to hear, to announce. The question imagines someone who must fetch the command and then teach it.

decisions.choice: to say: so that someone would have to say
decisions.reason: The infinitive gives the thought that would follow if the command were in heaven: people would be left asking who could fetch it.

decisions.choice: single quotation marks
decisions.reason: The question is quoted inside Moses' speech, so it takes single quotation marks.

decisions.choice: that you would need to ask / You do not need to ask
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable supply "you" as the one who would ask, and say "ask" for "say" before a question.

source.text: וְלֹֽא־מֵעֵ֥בֶר לַיָּ֖ם הִ֑וא לֵאמֹ֗ר מִ֣י יַעֲבָר־לָ֜נוּ אֶל־עֵ֤בֶר הַיָּם֙ וְיִקָּחֶ֣הָ לָּ֔נוּ וְיַשְׁמִעֵ֥נוּ אֹתָ֖הּ וְנַעֲשֶֽׂנָּה׃

records.literal_gloss: And not from [the] other side of the sea [is] it, to say, who will cross over for us to [the] other side of the sea and take it for us and make us hear it, and we will do it?

en.L: And it [is] not beyond the sea, to say, 'Who will cross over for us to the other side of the sea and take it for us and make us hear it, so that we may do it?'
en.B: Nor is it on the far side of the sea, that you would need to ask, 'Who will cross the sea for us and get it for us, and tell it to us so that we can do it?'
en.R: And it is not across the sea. You do not need to ask, 'Who will go over the sea to get it for us? Who will tell it to us so we can obey it?'

vi.L: Và nó không ở bên kia biển, để [ngươi] nói: 'Ai sẽ vượt qua bên kia biển cho chúng ta và lấy nó cho chúng ta, và cho chúng ta nghe nó, để chúng ta làm theo?'
vi.B: Nó cũng không ở bên kia biển, để anh em phải hỏi: 'Ai sẽ vượt biển lấy nó về cho chúng ta, và nói cho chúng ta nghe để chúng ta làm theo?'
vi.R: Nó cũng không ở bên kia biển. Anh em không cần phải hỏi: 'Ai sẽ vượt biển để lấy nó cho chúng ta? Ai sẽ nói cho chúng ta biết để chúng ta vâng theo?'

decisions.choice: beyond the sea: the farthest place across the water
decisions.reason: The far side of the sea pairs with heaven in verse 12: the farthest point across, as heaven is the farthest point up.

decisions.choice: Romans 10:7
decisions.reason: When Paul applies these verses to Christ, he puts "who will go down into the abyss", the depths, in place of the journey across the sea, and speaks of bringing Christ up from the dead (Romans 10:7).

decisions.choice: As in verse 12.
decisions.reason: The question is set out as in verse 12, with single quotation marks and the same supplied words at Balanced and Readable.

source.text: כִּֽי־קָר֥וֹב אֵלֶ֛יךָ הַדָּבָ֖ר מְאֹ֑ד בְּפִ֥יךָ וּבִֽלְבָבְךָ֖ לַעֲשֹׂתֽוֹ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: But near to you [is] the word very, in your mouth and in your heart, to do it.

en.L: But the word [is] very near to you, in your mouth and in your heart, to do it.
en.B: No, the word is very near you, in your mouth and in your heart, for you to do.
en.R: No, the word is very close to you. It is on your lips and in your heart, so you can obey it.

vi.L: Nhưng lời ấy rất gần ngươi, ở trong miệng ngươi và trong lòng ngươi, để ngươi làm theo.
vi.B: Không, lời ấy ở rất gần anh em, ở ngay trong miệng và trong lòng anh em, để anh em làm theo.
vi.R: Không, lời ấy ở rất gần anh em. Nó ở trên môi và trong lòng anh em, để anh em có thể vâng theo.

decisions.choice: in your mouth and in your heart: spoken aloud and known within
decisions.reason: Israel was to recite God's words, talking of them at home and on the road (6:6-7), and to keep them in the heart. The word is already theirs, in what they say and in what they think.

decisions.choice: Romans 10:8
decisions.reason: Paul quotes this verse and says that the word near you is "the word of faith that we proclaim": confessed with the mouth and believed in the heart (Romans 10:8-10).

decisions.choice: the word is near so that it can be done
decisions.reason: God has not hidden his will; he has spoken it and given it to his people (29:28). Because it is near, obeying it is possible.

decisions.choice: but: the answer to the two denials
decisions.reason: After "not in heaven" and "not beyond the sea", the word says where it really is.

decisions.choice: on your lips
decisions.reason: Readable uses the English idiom for words that are spoken; Literal and Balanced keep "mouth".

source.text: רְאֵ֨ה נָתַ֤תִּי לְפָנֶ֨יךָ֙ הַיּ֔וֹם אֶת־הַֽחַיִּ֖ים וְאֶת־הַטּ֑וֹב וְאֶת־הַמָּ֖וֶת וְאֶת־הָרָֽע׃

records.literal_gloss: See, I have set before you this day the life and the good, and the death and the evil.

en.L: See, I have set before you today life and good, and death and evil.
en.B: See, today I have placed before you life and good, death and harm.
en.R: Look! Today I am giving you a choice between life and good things, or death and bad things.

vi.L: Hãy xem, hôm nay tôi đã đặt trước mặt ngươi sự sống và điều tốt lành, sự chết và điều tai họa.
vi.B: Hãy xem, hôm nay tôi đặt trước mặt anh em sự sống và phước hạnh, sự chết và tai họa.
vi.R: Hãy nhìn đây! Hôm nay tôi cho anh em chọn lựa giữa sự sống và những điều tốt lành, hay sự chết và những điều tai hại.

decisions.choice: good and evil: well-being and harm
decisions.reason: Here "good" and "evil" are what happens to the people: prosperity and blessing, or disaster and ruin. They go with life and death, as blessing and curse do in verse 19.

decisions.choice: I have set: done by these very words
decisions.reason: The verb describes an act Moses performs by speaking. In laying out the covenant he puts the two ways before Israel now.

decisions.choice: set before you: the blessing and the curse of 11:26-28
decisions.reason: Moses said the same at the start of the laws (11:26-28): a blessing if they obey and a curse if they do not. Jeremiah later uses this picture of the way of life and the way of death (Jeremiah 21:8).

decisions.choice: harm
decisions.reason: Balanced says "harm" for "evil" here, since the word means what Israel would suffer, not moral wrong (m1). Literal keeps "evil".

decisions.choice: a choice between
decisions.reason: Readable makes explicit what verse 19 says outright: the things set before Israel are for it to choose between.

source.text: אֲשֶׁ֨ר אָנֹכִ֣י מְצַוְּךָ֮ הַיּוֹם֒ לְאַהֲבָ֞ה אֶת־יְהוָ֤ה אֱלֹהֶ֨יךָ֙ לָלֶ֣כֶת בִּדְרָכָ֔יו וְלִשְׁמֹ֛ר מִצְוֺתָ֥יו וְחֻקֹּתָ֖יו וּמִשְׁפָּטָ֑יו וְחָיִ֣יתָ וְרָבִ֔יתָ וּבֵֽרַכְךָ֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ בָּאָ֕רֶץ אֲשֶׁר־אַתָּ֥ה בָא־שָׁ֖מָּה לְרִשְׁתָּֽהּ׃

records.literal_gloss: [In] that I [am] commanding you this day to love Yahweh your God, to walk in his ways and to keep his commandments and his statutes and his judgments, and you will live and multiply, and will bless you Yahweh your God in the land where you [are] going there to take possession of it.

en.L: [In] that I [am] commanding you today to love {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, to walk in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} ways, and to keep {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} commandments and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} statutes and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} judgments, then you will live and multiply, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God will bless you in the land that you [are] going into to take possession of it.
en.B: For what I command you today is that you love {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, walk in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} ways, and keep {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} commandments, statutes and rulings. Then you will live and grow numerous, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God will bless you in the land you are entering to take possession of.
en.R: Today I am commanding you to love {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, to live the way {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} wants, and to obey {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} commands, laws and rules. If you do, you will live and there will be more and more of you. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} your God will bless you in the land you are going into to take possession of.

vi.L: [Ấy là] tôi truyền cho ngươi hôm nay phải yêu kính {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của ngươi, bước đi trong các đường lối {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, và giữ các điều răn {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, các luật lệ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} và các mạng lệnh {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, thì ngươi sẽ sống và gia tăng, và {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của ngươi sẽ ban phước cho ngươi trong xứ mà ngươi đang đi vào để chiếm hữu nó.
vi.B: Vì điều tôi truyền cho anh em hôm nay là hãy yêu kính {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của anh em, đi theo đường lối {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, giữ các điều răn, luật lệ và mạng lệnh của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Bấy giờ anh em sẽ được sống và thêm đông, và {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của anh em sẽ ban phước cho anh em trong xứ anh em sắp vào để chiếm lấy.
vi.R: Hôm nay tôi truyền cho anh em phải yêu kính {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của anh em, sống theo cách {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} muốn, và vâng giữ các điều răn, luật lệ và mạng lệnh của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Nếu anh em làm như vậy, anh em sẽ được sống và ngày càng đông thêm. {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của anh em sẽ ban phước cho anh em trong xứ anh em sắp vào để chiếm lấy.

decisions.choice: the Hebrew text: "in that I command you"
alternatives: If you obey the commandments of the LORD your God that I command you today, by loving ...
decisions.reason: The Hebrew begins with only "that" or "which". The ancient Greek translation reads a longer opening, "If you listen to the commandments of the LORD your God that I command you today, to love ...", which gives the verse a clear "if" to match "but if" in verse 17. The Hebrew text is followed here; reviewers should check the evidence.

decisions.choice: that I command you: the life and good of verse 15 explained
decisions.reason: The opening word ties this verse to verse 15. Life and good come by loving the LORD and keeping his ways, which is what Moses is commanding; the result follows: "then you will live".

decisions.choice: walk in his ways: live as he directs
decisions.reason: Life is pictured as a road. To walk in God's ways is to live the way he shows (8:6; 10:12; 11:22).

decisions.choice: commandments, statutes and judgments: the whole of God's law
decisions.reason: The three words together name everything Moses teaches: commands, fixed rules, and rulings on what is right (4:1; 5:31; 6:1).

decisions.choice: For what I command you today is
decisions.reason: Balanced opens with "For what I command you today is" to show that the verse explains verse 15; Literal brackets "[In]" to show how "that" links the two.

decisions.choice: live the way he wants; If you do
decisions.reason: Readable gives the sense of "walk in his ways" and states the condition that the Hebrew joins with "and".

source.text: וְאִם־יִפְנֶ֥ה לְבָבְךָ֖ וְלֹ֣א תִשְׁמָ֑ע וְנִדַּחְתָּ֗ וְהִֽשְׁתַּחֲוִ֛יתָ לֵאלֹהִ֥ים אֲחֵרִ֖ים וַעֲבַדְתָּֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And if turns away your heart and not you listen, and you are drawn away and bow down to gods other and serve them,

en.L: But if your heart turns away and you do not listen, and you are drawn away and bow down to other gods and serve them,
en.B: But if your heart turns away and you will not listen, and you are drawn away to bow down to other gods and serve them,
en.R: But your heart may turn away from {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and you may refuse to listen. You may let yourselves be drawn away to bow down to other gods and worship them.

vi.L: Nhưng nếu lòng ngươi quay đi và ngươi không nghe, và ngươi bị lôi cuốn mà quỳ lạy các thần khác và phục vụ chúng,
vi.B: Nhưng nếu lòng anh em quay đi, anh em không chịu nghe, và bị lôi cuốn đi quỳ lạy và phục vụ các thần khác,
vi.R: Nhưng có thể lòng anh em quay khỏi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, và anh em không chịu nghe. Có thể anh em để mình bị lôi cuốn đi quỳ lạy và thờ phượng các thần khác.

decisions.choice: drawn away: led astray, pulled aside
decisions.reason: It is the verb used of being driven out among the nations in verses 1 and 4. Being drawn away to other gods leads to being driven away from the land.

decisions.choice: bow down and serve: worship
decisions.reason: To bow down was the act of worship, and to serve a god was to give him loyalty and offerings. The pair is the language of the second commandment (5:9; 8:19; 11:16).

decisions.choice: but if: the second way, answered in verse 18
decisions.reason: Verse 16 gave the way of life; this verse gives the opposite, and verse 18 says what follows.

decisions.choice: from him; worship
decisions.reason: Readable says whom the heart turns away from and gives the plain word "worship" for "serve".

source.text: הִגַּ֤דְתִּי לָכֶם֙ הַיּ֔וֹם כִּ֥י אָבֹ֖ד תֹּאבֵד֑וּן לֹא־תַאֲרִיכֻ֤ן יָמִים֙ עַל־הָ֣אֲדָמָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר אַתָּ֤ה עֹבֵר֙ אֶת־הַיַּרְדֵּ֔ן לָבֹ֥אשָׁ֖מָּה לְרִשְׁתָּֽהּ׃

records.literal_gloss: I declare to you this day that perishing you will perish; not you will prolong days on the land where you [are] crossing the Jordan to go there to take possession of it.

en.L: I declare to you today that you will surely perish; you will not prolong [your] days on the land that you [are] crossing the Jordan to go into to take possession of it.
en.B: I tell you plainly today that you will certainly be destroyed. You will not live long in the land you are crossing the Jordan to enter and take possession of.
en.R: Then I am telling you today that you will surely be destroyed. You will not live long in the land you are crossing the Jordan River to take possession of.

vi.L: thì hôm nay tôi tuyên bố với các ngươi rằng các ngươi chắc chắn sẽ bị tiêu vong; các ngươi sẽ không được sống lâu trên đất mà ngươi đang qua sông Giô-đanh để vào chiếm hữu.
vi.B: thì hôm nay tôi nói rõ với anh em rằng anh em chắc chắn sẽ bị hủy diệt. Anh em sẽ không được sống lâu trong xứ mà anh em sắp qua sông Giô-đanh để vào chiếm lấy.
vi.R: Nếu vậy, hôm nay tôi nói cho anh em biết rằng anh em chắc chắn sẽ bị hủy diệt. Anh em sẽ không được sống lâu trong xứ anh em sắp qua sông Giô-đanh để chiếm lấy.

decisions.choice: perishing you will perish: certainty
decisions.reason: Hebrew repeats the verb to make a statement certain and strong, as in 4:26 and 8:19.

decisions.choice: you: plural, the whole people
decisions.reason: Moses has been speaking to Israel as "you" singular. Here he turns to the plural, to every one of them.

decisions.choice: prolong days: live long
decisions.reason: To lengthen days on the land is to live long there and keep it (4:26, 40).

decisions.choice: tell you plainly
decisions.reason: The verb means to make known, to declare openly. Balanced adds "plainly" to keep that force; Literal says "declare".

source.text: הַעִידֹ֨תִי בָכֶ֣ם הַיּוֹם֮ אֶת־הַשָּׁמַ֣יִם וְאֶת־הָאָרֶץ֒ הַחַיִּ֤ים וְהַמָּ֨וֶת֙ נָתַ֣תִּי לְפָנֶ֔יךָ הַבְּרָכָ֖ה וְהַקְּלָלָ֑ה וּבָֽחַרְתָּ֙ בַּֽחַיִּ֔ים לְמַ֥עַן תִּחְיֶ֖ה אַתָּ֥ה וְזַרְעֶֽךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: I call as witness against you this day the heavens and the earth: the life and the death I have set before you, the blessing and the curse; and you shall choose the life, so that you may live, you and your offspring,

en.L: I call the heavens and the earth to witness against you today: life and death I have set before you, the blessing and the curse. So choose life, so that you may live, you and your offspring,
en.B: Today I call heaven and earth to testify against you: I have set before you life and death, blessing and curse. So choose life, that you and your descendants may live,
en.R: Today I am calling the sky and the earth to be witnesses against you. I have given you a choice between life and death, between blessing and curse. Choose life! Then you and your descendants will live.

vi.L: Hôm nay tôi gọi trời và đất làm chứng nghịch lại các ngươi: sự sống và sự chết tôi đã đặt trước mặt ngươi, phước lành và sự nguyền rủa. Vậy hãy chọn sự sống, để ngươi được sống, ngươi và dòng dõi ngươi,
vi.B: Hôm nay tôi gọi trời và đất làm chứng nghịch lại anh em rằng tôi đã đặt trước mặt anh em sự sống và sự chết, phước lành và sự nguyền rủa. Vậy hãy chọn sự sống, để anh em và dòng dõi anh em được sống,
vi.R: Hôm nay tôi gọi trời và đất làm chứng nghịch lại anh em. Tôi đã cho anh em chọn lựa giữa sự sống và sự chết, giữa phước lành và sự nguyền rủa. Hãy chọn sự sống! Khi ấy anh em và con cháu anh em sẽ được sống.

decisions.choice: heaven and earth as witnesses: the witnesses of a covenant
decisions.reason: Treaties of the time named witnesses who would see that the terms were kept. Moses calls on heaven and earth, which last from one generation to the next (4:26; 31:28; 32:1).

decisions.choice: and you shall choose: an urgent call to decide
decisions.reason: The verb form follows from what comes before: since life and death are set before them, Israel is to choose. It is an appeal, not a forecast.

decisions.choice: choose life: the full life with God in the land
decisions.reason: Life here is more than staying alive. It is the life of a people that loves the LORD and lives long in the land he gives (verses 16, 20; 4:1).

decisions.choice: life and death first: stress on the choice
decisions.reason: The Hebrew puts "the life and the death" before the verb to stress what is at stake.

decisions.choice: descendants
decisions.reason: As in verse 6.

decisions.choice: a choice between
decisions.reason: As in verse 15, Readable says that the two are set before Israel to choose between.

source.text: לְאַֽהֲבָה֙ אֶת־יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ לִשְׁמֹ֥עַ בְּקֹל֖וֹ וּלְדָבְקָה־ב֑וֹ כִּ֣י ה֤וּא חַיֶּ֨יךָ֙ וְאֹ֣רֶךְ יָמֶ֔יךָ לָשֶׁ֣בֶת עַל־הָאֲדָמָ֗ה אֲשֶׁר֩ נִשְׁבַּ֨ע יְהוָ֧ה לַאֲבֹתֶ֛יךָ לְאַבְרָהָ֛ם לְיִצְחָ֥ק וּֽלְיַעֲקֹ֖ב לָתֵ֥ת לָהֶֽם׃פ

records.literal_gloss: to love Yahweh your God, to listen to his voice and to cling to him, for he [is] your life and [the] length of your days, to dwell on the land that swore Yahweh to your fathers, to Abraham, to Isaac and to Jacob, to give to them.

en.L: to love {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, to listen to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} voice, and to cling to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}; for {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} [is] your life and the length of your days, to dwell on the land that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} swore to your fathers, to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob, to give them."
en.B: by loving {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, obeying {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and holding fast to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. For {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is your life and your long years, so that you may live in the land that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} swore to give to your ancestors, Abraham, Isaac and Jacob."
en.R: Love {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, obey {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and hold on to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. He is your life, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will give you long life in the land {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} promised with an oath to give your ancestors Abraham, Isaac and Jacob."

vi.L: [bằng cách] yêu kính {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của ngươi, nghe theo tiếng {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} và gắn bó với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}; vì {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} [là] sự sống của ngươi và sự lâu dài của các ngày ngươi, để ngươi được ở trên đất mà {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã thề với tổ phụ ngươi, với Áp-ra-ham, với Y-sác và với Gia-cốp, là sẽ ban cho họ."
vi.B: bằng cách yêu kính {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của anh em, vâng theo {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} và gắn bó với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Vì chính {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} là sự sống của anh em và ban cho anh em được sống lâu, để anh em được ở trong xứ mà {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã thề ban cho tổ tiên anh em là Áp-ra-ham, Y-sác và Gia-cốp."
vi.R: Hãy yêu kính {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của anh em, vâng lời {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} và bám chặt lấy {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Ngài là sự sống của anh em, và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sẽ cho anh em được sống lâu trong xứ mà {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã thề hứa ban cho tổ tiên anh em là Áp-ra-ham, Y-sác và Gia-cốp."

decisions.choice: to love: what choosing life means
decisions.reason: The three infinitives, to love, to listen and to cling, spell out how Israel chooses life: by loving the LORD and staying loyal to him.

decisions.choice: cling: hold fast, stay joined
decisions.reason: The verb is used of a man joined to his wife (Genesis 2:24) and of Ruth clinging to Naomi (Ruth 1:14). Held to the LORD, it means loyal, lasting closeness (10:20; 11:22; 13:5).

decisions.choice: he is your life: the LORD himself is Israel's life
alternatives: that is your life and the length of your days
decisions.reason: The pronoun most naturally points back to the LORD, the one Israel loves and clings to. It can also be read "that is your life": loving and clinging to him is life for Israel. Either way life and long days are found in him.

decisions.choice: the land sworn to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob
decisions.reason: The speech closes where Deuteronomy began, with the land the LORD promised on oath to the patriarchs (1:8; Genesis 12:7; 26:3; 28:13).

decisions.choice: the end of Moses' speech
decisions.reason: The speech that began at 29:1 ends here. Chapter 31 goes back to the narrator.

decisions.choice: the closing quotation mark
decisions.reason: The double quotation mark opened at 29:1 closes at the end of this verse, where Moses' speech ends.

decisions.choice: by loving / Love; your long years / he will give you long life
decisions.reason: Balanced shows with "by" that the infinitives explain "choose life", and says "your long years" for "the length of your days". Readable makes the infinitives a direct appeal and says what "the length of your days, to dwell on the land" means.

decisions.choice: "[bằng cách]" links verse 20 to "choose life"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew infinitives say what choosing life means; Vietnamese needs a link word to show it.
